statement: One line holds a non-negative integer n. Print how many digits n has. The digit loop does it with arithmetic alone: while n is positive, divide it by 10 (integer division) and count one pass - each division drops the rightmost digit. Mind the special case: 0 has one digit, but a while-positive loop runs zero times on it, so guard it explicitly or use a do-while shape.

example.why: The loop sees 5678, 567, 56, 5 and then 0 - four passes, four digits.

hint: Count passes, nothing else - the digits' values are irrelevant to their count.
mistake: Returning 0 for n = 0 because the loop body ran zero times; zero is a one-digit number.
